    16	module cc_fifo #(
    17	    parameter bit          FallThrough = 1'b0, // fifo is in fall-through mode
    18	    parameter int unsigned DataWidth   = 32,   // default data width if the fifo is of type logic
    19	    parameter int unsigned Depth       = 8,    // depth can be arbitrary from 0 to 2**32
    20	    parameter type         data_t      = logic [DataWidth-1:0],
    21	    // DO NOT OVERWRITE THIS PARAMETER
    22	    localparam int unsigned UsageWidth = cc_pkg::cnt_width(Depth)
    23	)(
    24	    input  logic  clk_i,   // Clock
    25	    input  logic  rst_ni,  // Asynchronous reset active low
    26	    input  logic  clr_i,   // Synchronous clear active high; clears internal pointers *and*
    27	                           // memories.
    28	    input  logic  flush_i, // Flush the queue; compared to clr_i this only clears internal pointers.
    29	                           // Sufficient for most functional purposes.
    30	    // Status flags
    31	    output logic  full_o,  // Queue is full
    32	    output logic  empty_o, // Queue is empty
    33	    output logic  [UsageWidth-1:0] usage_o,  // Fill pointer
    34	    // As long as the queue is not full we can push new data
    35	    input  data_t data_i,  // Data to push into the queue
    36	    input  logic  push_i,  // Data is valid and can be pushed to the queue
    37	    // As long as the queue is not empty we can pop new elements
    38	    output data_t data_o,  // Output data
    39	    input  logic  pop_i    // Pop head from queue
    40	);
    41	    // local parameter
    42	    // FIFO depth - handle the case of pass-through, synthesizer will do constant propagation
    43	    localparam int unsigned FifoDepth = (Depth > 0) ? Depth : 1;
    44	    localparam int unsigned PtrWidth = cc_pkg::idx_width(Depth);
    45	    // clock gating control
    46	    logic gate_clock;
    47	    // pointer to the read and write section of the queue
    48	    logic [PtrWidth-1:0] read_pointer_n, read_pointer_q, write_pointer_n, write_pointer_q;
    49	    // keep a counter to keep track of the current queue status
    50	    // this integer will be truncated by the synthesis tool
    51	    logic [UsageWidth-1:0] status_cnt_n, status_cnt_q;
    52	    // actual memory
    53	    data_t [FifoDepth - 1:0] mem_n, mem_q;
    54	
    55	    assign usage_o = status_cnt_q;
    56	
    57	    if (Depth == 0) begin : gen_pass_through
    58	        assign empty_o     = ~push_i;
    59	        assign full_o      = ~pop_i;
    60	    end else begin : gen_fifo
    61	        assign full_o       = (status_cnt_q == FifoDepth[UsageWidth-1:0]);
    62	        assign empty_o      = (status_cnt_q == 0) & ~(FallThrough & push_i);
    63	    end
    64	    // status flags
    65	
    66	    // read and write queue logic
    67	    always_comb begin : read_write_comb
    68	        // default assignment
    69	        read_pointer_n  = read_pointer_q;
    70	        write_pointer_n = write_pointer_q;
    71	        status_cnt_n    = status_cnt_q;
    72	        data_o          = (Depth == 0) ? data_i : mem_q[read_pointer_q];
    73	        mem_n           = mem_q;
    74	        gate_clock      = 1'b1;
    75	
    76	        // push a new element to the queue
    77	        if (push_i && ~full_o) begin
    78	            // push the data onto the queue
    79	            mem_n[write_pointer_q] = data_i;
    80	            // un-gate the clock, we want to write something
    81	            gate_clock = 1'b0;
    82	            // increment the write counter
    83	            // this is dead code when Depth is a power of two
    84	            if (write_pointer_q == FifoDepth[PtrWidth-1:0] - 1)
    85	                write_pointer_n = '0;
    86	            else
    87	                write_pointer_n = write_pointer_q + 1;
    88	            // increment the overall counter
    89	            status_cnt_n    = status_cnt_q + 1;
    90	        end
    91	
    92	        if (pop_i && ~empty_o) begin
    93	            // read from the queue is a default assignment
    94	            // but increment the read pointer...
    95	            // this is dead code when Depth is a power of two
    96	            if (read_pointer_n == FifoDepth[PtrWidth-1:0] - 1)
    97	                read_pointer_n = '0;
    98	            else
    99	                read_pointer_n = read_pointer_q + 1;
   100	            // ... and decrement the overall count
   101	            status_cnt_n   = status_cnt_q - 1;
   102	        end
   103	
   104	        // keep the count pointer stable if we push and pop at the same time
   105	        if (push_i && pop_i &&  ~full_o && ~empty_o)
   106	            status_cnt_n   = status_cnt_q;
   107	
   108	        // FIFO is in pass through mode -> do not change the pointers
   109	        if (FallThrough && (status_cnt_q == 0) && push_i) begin
   110	            data_o = data_i;
   111	            if (pop_i) begin
   112	                status_cnt_n = status_cnt_q;
   113	                read_pointer_n = read_pointer_q;
   114	                write_pointer_n = write_pointer_q;
   115	            end
   116	        end
   117	    end
   118	
   119	    // sequential process
   120	    logic clr_or_flush;
   121	    assign clr_or_flush = clr_i || flush_i;
   122	    `FFARNC(read_pointer_q, read_pointer_n, clr_or_flush, '0, clk_i, rst_ni)
   123	    `FFARNC(write_pointer_q, write_pointer_n, clr_or_flush, '0, clk_i, rst_ni)
   124	    `FFARNC(status_cnt_q, status_cnt_n, clr_or_flush, '0, clk_i, rst_ni)
   125	
   126	    `FFLARNC(mem_q, mem_n, !gate_clock, clr_i, {FifoDepth{data_t'('0)}}, clk_i, rst_ni)
   127

   129	    `ASSERT_INIT(depth_0, Depth > 0, "Depth must be greater than 0.")
   130	
   131	    `ASSERT(full_write, full_o |-> ~push_i, clk_i, !rst_ni,
   132	            "Trying to push new data although the FIFO is full.")
   133	
   134	    `ASSERT(empty_read, empty_o |-> ~pop_i, clk_i, !rst_ni,
   135	            "Trying to pop data although the FIFO is empty.")
   136	`endif

    12	module floo_vc_arbiter import floo_pkg::*;

    15	  parameter type         flit_t           = logic,
    16	  parameter int unsigned NumPhysChannels  = 1,
    17	  parameter vc_impl_e    VcImpl           = VcNaive,

    24	  output logic  [NumVirtChannels-1:0] ready_o,
    25	  input  flit_t [NumVirtChannels-1:0] data_i,

    35	  assign ready_o = ready_i;

    37	end else if (NumPhysChannels == 1) begin : gen_single_phys

    43	    logic                       vc_arb_req_out, vc_arb_gnt_in;
    44	
    45	    // Signals to support credit based arbitration
    46	    logic [NumVirtChannels-1:0] credit_handshake, credit_left;
    47	
    48	    // Mask used to switch VC requests
    49	    logic [NumVirtChannels-1:0] mask_q, mask_d;

    52	    // Lock and mask update logic //
    53	    ////////////////////////////////
    54	
    55	    if (VcImpl == VcPreemptValid) begin: gen_preempt_valid_mask
    56	      always_comb begin
    57	        mask_d = mask_q;

    59	        // other VC has a grant, switch VC in the next cycle. This logic works with only two VCs

    62	          if (!vc_arb_gnt_in) begin

    69	        end
    70	      end

    80	      // Initially, any valid channel can request access to the physical channel.

    12	  /// Currently Supported Routing Algorithms
    13	  typedef enum logic[2:0] {
    14	    /// `IdTable` routing uses a table of routing rules to determine to
    15	    /// which output port a packet should be routed, based on the
    16	    /// destination ID encoded in the header of the flit. Every router
    17	    /// needs its own table, that is passed to `id_route_map_i`. The
    18	    /// network interface only needs to convert the physical address to
    19	    /// the destination ID, that is later used by the routers.
    20	    IdTable,
    21	    /// `SourceRouting` calculates the route to the destination in the
    22	    /// source itself (i.e. the network interfaces). The route is encoded
    23	    /// as a sequence of router ports that the packet should traverse. At
    24	    /// every router hop, a port is popped from the route list. The routes
    25	    /// need to be passed to the network interfaces `route_table_i`, which
    26	    /// is a table of routes that can be indexed with the destination ID.
    27	    /// This algorithm is mainly useful for smaller networks with fewer
    28	    /// hops where the encoding size of the route does not become too large.
    29	    SourceRouting,
    30	    /// `XYRouting` is a simple routing algorithm that routes packets
    31	    /// based on the XY coordinates of current and destination node. Every
    32	    /// router needs to be aware of its own XY coordinates and forwards
    33	    /// packets based on the difference of the coordinates. The network
    34	    /// interface needs to convert the physical address to the destination
    35	    ///  XY coordinates, which can be done with addressoffsets `XYAddrOffsetX`
    36	    /// and `XYAddrOffsetY`, or by indexing the system address map `Sam`. This
    37	    /// is controlled with the `UseIdTable` parameter.
    38	    XYRouting,
    39	    /// `YXRouting` is identical to `XYRouting` but resolves the Y dimension first,
    40	    /// then the X dimension.
    41	    YXRouting,
    42	    /// `XYRoutingMirrored` is only meaningful for `floo_nw_router`: the
    43	    /// narrow/wide-write request path uses `XYRouting`, while the
    44	    /// narrow/wide-read response path uses `YXRouting`. Only legal when the
    45	    /// wide channel is physically decoupled (`WideRwDecouple == Phys`).
    46	    XYRoutingMirrored,
    47	    /// `YXRoutingMirrored` is the mirror image of `XYRoutingMirrored`: the
    48	    /// request path uses `YXRouting`, the response path uses `XYRouting`.
    49	    YXRoutingMirrored
    50	  } route_algo_e;

    52	  /// True for any dimension-ordered routing algorithm (`XYRouting`,
    53	  /// `YXRouting`, or one of the mirrored variants).
    54	  function automatic bit is_dor_algo(route_algo_e algo);
    55	    return algo == XYRouting || algo == YXRouting ||
    56	           algo == XYRoutingMirrored || algo == YXRoutingMirrored;
    57	  endfunction

    59	  /// Concrete routing algorithm used by request-like paths for a possibly mirrored algorithm.
    60	  function automatic route_algo_e route_algo_req(route_algo_e algo);
    61	    unique case (algo)
    62	      XYRoutingMirrored: return XYRouting;
    63	      YXRoutingMirrored: return YXRouting;
    64	      default:           return algo;
    65	    endcase
    66	  endfunction

    69	  function automatic route_algo_e route_algo_rsp(route_algo_e algo);
    70	    unique case (algo)
    71	      XYRoutingMirrored: return YXRouting;

   539	  /// These functions help to abstract the complexity of the NoC and the
   540	  /// implementation schemes for collective communication.
   541	  /// The user is responsible to declare only which macro level collective
   542	  /// operations are supported in the NoC (collect_op_fe_cfg_t).
   543	  /// The NoC implementation will then derive which type of hardware support
   544	  /// is required (e.g. multicast, collectB, selectAW, etc...). This info
   545	  /// is implementation specific and must be transparent to the user.
   546	  ///
   547	  /// Helper functions to calculate which macro operations are supported
   548	  /// and which type of hardware support is required
   549	
   550	  /// Calculates if the NoC needs support for Narrow sequential reduction
   551	  function automatic bit en_narrow_seq_reduction(collect_op_fe_cfg_t cfg);
   552	    return (cfg.EnIntAdd | cfg.EnIntMul | cfg.EnIntMinS |
   553	            cfg.EnIntMinU | cfg.EnIntMaxS | cfg.EnIntMaxU
   554	            );
   555	  endfunction
   556	
   557	  /// Calculates if the NoC needs support for Narrow Sequential reduction
   558	  function automatic bit en_narrow_reduction(collect_op_fe_cfg_t cfg);
   559	    return (en_narrow_seq_reduction(cfg) | cfg.EnLsbAnd
   560	            );
   561	  endfunction
   562	
   563	  /// Calculates if the NoC needs support for Wide Sequential reduction
   564	  /// there is no need to separate between parallel and sequential for the
   565	  /// wide because only wide sequential is supported
   566	  function automatic bit en_wide_reduction(collect_op_fe_cfg_t cfg);
   567	    return (cfg.EnFpAdd | cfg.EnFpMul |
   568	            cfg.EnFpMin | cfg.EnFpMax
   569	            );
   570	  endfunction
   571	
   572	  /// Calculate if narrow collective support is enabled
   573	  function automatic bit en_narrow_collective(collect_op_fe_cfg_t cfg);
   574	    return (cfg.EnNarrowMulticast | en_narrow_reduction(cfg));
   575	  endfunction
   576	
   577	  /// Calculate if wide collective support is enabled
   578	  function automatic bit en_wide_collective(collect_op_fe_cfg_t cfg);
   579	    return (cfg.EnWideMulticast | en_wide_reduction(cfg));
   580	  endfunction
   581	
   582	  /// Calculate if there is need for collective support
   583	  function automatic bit en_collective(collect_op_fe_cfg_t cfg);
   584	    return (en_wide_collective(cfg) | en_narrow_collective(cfg));
   585	  endfunction
   586	
   587	  /// Helper functions to calculate which micro transaction are supported
   588	  /// and which type of hardware support is required
   589	  function automatic bit en_sequential_support(collect_op_be_cfg_t cfg);
   590	    return (cfg.EnFpAdd | cfg.EnFpMul | cfg.EnFpMin | cfg.EnFpMax |
   591	            cfg.EnIntAdd | cfg.EnIntMul | cfg.EnIntMinS | cfg.EnIntMinU |
   592	            cfg.EnIntMaxS | cfg.EnIntMaxU
   593	            );
   594	  endfunction
   595	
   596	  function automatic bit en_parallel_support(collect_op_be_cfg_t cfg);
   597	    return (cfg.EnLsbAnd | cfg.EnCollectB | cfg.EnSelectAW);
   598	  endfunction
   599	
   600	  function automatic bit en_multicast_support(collect_op_be_cfg_t cfg);
   601	    return (cfg.EnMulticast);
   602	  endfunction
   603	
   604	  /// Helper functions to translate internal opcodes in macro transactions
   605	  /// Evaluate if the incoming operation is a multicast operation
   606	  function automatic bit is_multicast_op(collect_op_e op);
   607	    return (op == Multicast);
   608	  endfunction
   609	
   610	  /// Evaluate if the incoming operation is a reduction operation
   611	  function automatic bit is_reduction_op(collect_op_e op);
   612	    case (op)
   613	      FpAdd, FpMul, FpMin, FpMax, LsbAnd, SelectAW, SeqAW,
   614	      IntAdd, IntMul, IntMinS, IntMinU, IntMaxS,
   615	      IntMaxU: return 1'b1;
   616	      default: return 1'b0;
   617	    endcase
   618	  endfunction
   619	
   620	  /// Evaluate if the incoming operation is a parallel reduction
   621	  function automatic bit is_parallel_reduction_op(collect_op_e op);
   622	    return (op == LsbAnd || op == CollectB || op == SelectAW);
   623	  endfunction
   624	
   625	  /// Evaluate if the incoming operation is a sequential reduction
   626	  function automatic bit is_seq_reduction_op(collect_op_e op);
   627	    case (op)
   628	      FpAdd, FpMul, FpMin, FpMax, SeqAW,
   629	      IntAdd, IntMul, IntMinS, IntMinU, IntMaxS,
   630	      IntMaxU: return 1'b1;
   631	      default: return 1'b0;
   632	    endcase
   633	  endfunction
   634	
   635	  /// Helper function to map frontend collective ops to backend config for NW routers.
   636	  /// The target router/link is identified by the AXI channel `ch` that traverses it
   637	  /// (via nw_chan_mapping): FlooReq carries narrow writes/reads and wide reads,
   638	  /// FlooRsp carries narrow responses, FlooWide carries wide writes/reads.
   639	  function automatic collect_op_be_cfg_t coll_fe2be(collect_op_fe_cfg_t fe_ops, nw_ch_e ch);
   640	    collect_op_be_cfg_t be = '0;
   641	    case (nw_chan_mapping(ch))
   642	      FlooReq: begin
   643	        /// - FP operations are not supported on the request link
   644	        /// - CollectB is not supported on the request link
   645	        be.EnMulticast = fe_ops.EnNarrowMulticast;
   646	        be.EnLsbAnd    = fe_ops.EnLsbAnd;
   647	        be.EnIntAdd     = fe_ops.EnIntAdd;
   648	        be.EnIntMul     = fe_ops.EnIntMul;
   649	        be.EnIntMinS   = fe_ops.EnIntMinS;
   650	        be.EnIntMinU   = fe_ops.EnIntMinU;
   651	        be.EnIntMaxS   = fe_ops.EnIntMaxS;
   652	        be.EnIntMaxU   = fe_ops.EnIntMaxU;
   653	        be.EnSelectAW  = fe_ops.EnLsbAnd;
   654	      end
   655	      /// - Arithmetic reductions are not supported on the response link
   656	      /// - Multicast necessary only to route reduction responses back
   657	      /// - CollectB necessary only to join multicast responses
   658	      FlooRsp: begin
   659	        be.EnMulticast = en_narrow_reduction(fe_ops) | en_wide_reduction(fe_ops);
   660	        be.EnCollectB  = fe_ops.EnNarrowMulticast | fe_ops.EnWideMulticast;
   661	      end
   662	      /// - ALU operations are not supported on the wide link
   663	      /// - CollectB is not supported on the wide link
   664	      FlooWide: begin
   665	        be.EnMulticast = fe_ops.EnWideMulticast;
   666	        be.EnFpAdd     = fe_ops.EnFpAdd;
   667	        be.EnFpMul     = fe_ops.EnFpMul;
   668	        be.EnFpMin     = fe_ops.EnFpMin;
   669	        be.EnFpMax     = fe_ops.EnFpMax;
   670	      end
   671	      default: be = '0;
   672	    endcase
   673	    return be;
   674	  endfunction

    17	  /// Returns the quotient of two natural numbers, rounded towards plus infinity.

    23

item.text: The configured top has three parameterized `floo_fifo` instances: nonzero-depth virtual and physical cases plus a depth-zero bypass. I’ve traced their generate paths and the FIFO implementation’s width/clear logic.

`flit_t` is packed to 23 bits (13 payload + 8 tag + 2 flags) ([top.sv:3](/private/tmp/slang-compare/runs/floo_config/text-only/rep_1/workspace/rtl/top.sv:3)). Widths below are flattened packed-port widths.

| `floo_fifo` subtree | Effective `(NumChannels, NumVirtChannels, NumPhysChannels, FifoDepth)` | `data_i` width | `valid_i` width | Selected generate branch | `cc_stream_fifo` / `floo_vc_arbiter` instances |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|
| `u_virtual` | `(3,4,1,5)` | `23×3×1 = 69` | `3×4 = 12` | `gen_floo_fifo.gen_virt_channels` | 12 / 3 |
| `u_physical` | `(2,3,3,2)` | `23×2×3 = 138` | `2×3 = 6` | `gen_floo_fifo.gen_phys_channels` | 6 / 0 |
| `u_bypass` | `(2,4,1,0)` | `23×2×1 = 46` | `2×4 = 8` | `gen_no_fifo` | 0 / 0 |

The overrides are at [top.sv:9](/private/tmp/slang-compare/runs/floo_config/text-only/rep_1/workspace/rtl/top.sv:9), [top.sv:14](/private/tmp/slang-compare/runs/floo_config/text-only/rep_1/workspace/rtl/top.sv:14), and [top.sv:19](/private/tmp/slang-compare/runs/floo_config/text-only/rep_1/workspace/rtl/top.sv:19); port shapes and generation are in [floo_fifo.sv:19](/private/tmp/slang-compare/runs/floo_config/text-only/rep_1/workspace/rtl/floo_fifo.sv:19).

Generate precedence is: depth zero selects `gen_no_fifo` first; only nonzero depths enter `gen_floo_fifo`. There, `NumPhysChannels == 1` is tested before `NumVirtChannels == NumPhysChannels` ([floo_fifo.sv:28](/private/tmp/slang-compare/runs/floo_config/text-only/rep_1/workspace/rtl/floo_fifo.sv:28)). Thus the bypass never reaches either inner branch, and a hypothetical nonzero configuration satisfying both inner predicates would select `gen_virt_channels`.

- Virtual `n=2, v=3` stream FIFO:

  `floo_config_top.u_virtual.gen_floo_fifo.gen_virt_channels.gen_channel[2].gen_virt_channel[3].i_stream_fifo`

  Effective `Depth=5`, `FallThrough=1'b0`. The source uses `.data_i(data_i[n])` and `.data_o(data_out[n][v])`; after genvar substitution these are `data_i[2]` and `data_out[2][3]`, respectively ([floo_fifo.sv:43](/private/tmp/slang-compare/runs/floo_config/text-only/rep_1/workspace/rtl/floo_fifo.sv:43)).

- Physical `n=1, v=2` stream FIFO:

  `floo_config_top.u_physical.gen_floo_fifo.gen_phys_channels.gen_channel[1].gen_virt_channel[2].i_stream_fifo`

  Effective `Depth=2`. The source expressions are `.data_i(data_i[n][v])` and `.data_o(data_o[n][v])`, becoming `data_i[1][2]` and `data_o[1][2]` ([floo_fifo.sv:80](/private/tmp/slang-compare/runs/floo_config/text-only/rep_1/workspace/rtl/floo_fifo.sv:80)).

For the virtual FIFO’s child

`…gen_channel[2].gen_virt_channel[3].i_stream_fifo.fifo_i`,

`PtrWidth = idx_width(5) = $clog2(5) = 3`, and the counter/usage width is `cnt_width(5) = idx_width(6) = $clog2(6) = 3` ([cc_pkg.sv:43](/private/tmp/slang-compare/runs/floo_config/text-only/rep_1/workspace/rtl/cc_pkg.sv:43)). `FifoDepth` is 5, and `mem_q` is five 23-bit packed flits: `5 × (13+8+2) = 115` packed bits ([cc_fifo.sv:43](/private/tmp/slang-compare/runs/floo_config/text-only/rep_1/workspace/rtl/cc_fifo.sv:43)). Although `cc_stream_fifo`’s `DataWidth` default is 32, this instance explicitly overrides `data_t` with the 23-bit struct; `mem_q` uses `data_t`, not a forced 32-bit element width.

The `floo_fifo` declaration defaults are `(2,1,1,1)` and scalar `logic` flits (1 bit) ([floo_fifo.sv:8](/private/tmp/slang-compare/runs/floo_config/text-only/rep_1/workspace/rtl/floo_fifo.sv:8)). Those defaults do not describe any of these integration instances; all three override the channel/depth values and use the 23-bit `flit_t`.

`clr_i` is not explicitly connected on either generated `cc_stream_fifo` template; only `flush_i` is tied to `1'b0` ([floo_fifo.sv:47](/private/tmp/slang-compare/runs/floo_config/text-only/rep_1/workspace/rtl/floo_fifo.sv:47), [floo_fifo.sv:84](/private/tmp/slang-compare/runs/floo_config/text-only/rep_1/workspace/rtl/floo_fifo.sv:84)). The stream FIFO definition is present, declares `clr_i`, and forwards it to `cc_fifo` ([cc_stream_fifo.sv:13](/private/tmp/slang-compare/runs/floo_config/text-only/rep_1/workspace/rtl/cc_stream_fifo.sv:13)). Internally, `clr_i` clears pointers/status with `flush_i`, while memory clearing uses `clr_i` itself ([cc_fifo.sv:121](/private/tmp/slang-compare/runs/floo_config/text-only/rep_1/workspace/rtl/cc_fifo.sv:121)). Therefore this is an omitted-input-connection issue, not a missing FIFO definition; the fragment provides no explicit known drive that would guarantee or disable clear behavior.
